hero.headline: Trump says US considering taking equity stakes in major AI companies
hero.body:
President Trump said the federal government is exploring whether to take ownership stakes in leading artificial intelligence companies, a shift from the traditional hands-off approach the US has long taken toward the technology sector. The administration has begun preliminary talks with OpenAI about a potential government stake in the AI startup.

Trump indicated the administration may move forward with profit-sharing arrangements with AI companies within the coming week. Under such an arrangement, the government would receive partial ownership in exchange for providing support or access to computing resources. Officials have described the approach as a mechanism to ensure the public benefits from AI development while preserving American leadership in the field.

The proposal has attracted commentary from across the political spectrum. Senator Bernie Sanders published an opinion piece arguing that artificial intelligence should be treated as a public resource, suggesting that citizens should own half of AI companies. The idea represents a significant departure from the low-regulation stance that has shaped US technology policy for decades.

The timing reflects broader questions emerging about how AI development should be regulated, how it should be governed to protect public safety, and who should gain financially from technological breakthroughs. OpenAI, valued at more than 100 billion dollars in private fundraising rounds, has received substantial investments from Microsoft and other private capital sources. Adding federal ownership would introduce government involvement into an industry sector that has been built primarily through private investment.

The administration has not disclosed potential details about any government equity positions, including their size, structure, or which companies beyond OpenAI might participate. The legal and regulatory mechanisms for establishing such arrangements remain uncertain, as does the specific process through which the government would obtain equity. Policy experts expect the proposal will face scrutiny from Congress and will raise complex questions about the appropriate boundaries between government involvement in private industry and maintaining fair market competition.

The discussions highlight the growing importance of artificial intelligence to national economic strategy and security. As AI companies have attracted unprecedented levels of private investment and achieved enormous valuations, policymakers have increasingly focused on questions about public benefit and national interest.

The proposal also comes as the Trump administration is developing broader strategies for AI policy. The administration has announced plans to meet with major AI companies to discuss the potential profit-sharing framework within the coming week, signaling the priority the White House places on these discussions.

Whether Congress would approve legislative changes needed to enable direct government equity ownership in private companies, and what constitutional questions might arise from such arrangements, remain unclear. The proposal will likely generate significant debate among lawmakers, economists, and technology industry representatives about the proper role of government in directing private sector development.

cards.headline: US Shoots Down Iranian Drones Over Strait of Hormuz After Strike on Radar Sites
cards.body:
The United States military shot down an Iranian drone that approached the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea, according to US Central Command. An F-35C fighter jet fired on the Iranian Shahed-139 unmanned aircraft after it flew toward the carrier "with unclear intent," the military said on Tuesday.

"An F-35C fighter jet from Abraham Lincoln shot down the Iranian drone in self-defence and to protect the aircraft carrier and personnel on board," said Captain Tim Hawkins, a navy spokesperson at Central Command. No American service members were injured and no equipment was damaged in the incident.

Iran's UN mission did not comment on the US account. Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that connection had been lost with a drone in international waters but stated the reason was unknown. The semi-official Fars news agency claimed an Iranian drone had completed a surveillance mission in international waters.

On the same day, the Iranian Revolutionary Guards harassed a US-flagged merchant vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Two IRGC boats and an Iranian Mohajer drone approached the tanker M/V Stena Imperative at high speeds and threatened to board and seize the ship, according to Central Command.

The military escalation comes as diplomats work to arrange nuclear negotiations between the countries. Donald Trump said that "bad things" would probably happen unless a deal could be reached, with US warships heading toward Iran. However, Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian instructed the country's foreign minister to "pursue fair and equitable negotiations" with the US, signaling Tehran's willingness to engage.

The White House confirmed that Trump envoy Steve Witkoff plans to hold talks with Iranian officials later in the week despite the drone incident, according to press secretary Karoline Leavitt. Iran's foreign ministry said consultations were still underway on the meeting location, with Turkey and Oman both expressing readiness to host discussions focused on nuclear issues.

Pezeshkian's announcement represented a significant shift for the reformist president, who had previously said the situation in Iran had gone beyond his control. His stance appeared to have support from Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who had previously dismissed talks.

The Lincoln carrier strike group represents the most visible element of a US military buildup in the Middle East following a violent crackdown against anti-government demonstrations in Iran last month. The buildup came after Trump demanded Tehran make nuclear concessions and sent additional military forces to the region. Trump previously stated Iran was "seriously talking" about a potential deal.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Ordering Village Evacuations
cards.teaser: Israeli forces conducted strikes in southern Lebanon after ordering evacuations of nine villages amid ongoing military operations.
cards.body:
Israel carried out military strikes in southern Lebanon after ordering the evacuation of nine villages. The United States announced a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon on Wednesday night following fresh talks, but Hezbollah rejected the proposed deal.

During the strikes, a U.N. peacekeeper with UNIFIL, the peacekeeping mission in Lebanon, was killed and others were wounded by mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon. US-Iran talks continue amid the escalating conflict in the region.

cards.headline: Nasdaq drops 4.2% in worst day of year as chip stocks fall
cards.teaser: Major stock indexes tumbled as semiconductor stocks led a broad technology selloff amid concerns about interest rates.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq Composite declined 4.2 percent on Friday, marking its worst single day of the year. The S&P 500 also posted its worst performance of 2026, with broad losses across Wall Street as chip stocks fell sharply.

The selloff intensified following strong jobs data that raised expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases. Technology and AI-related stocks bore the brunt of the decline as investors reassessed valuations in the sector amid shifting economic conditions.

cards.headline: FDA Unable to Identify Cause of Baby Botulism Outbreak or Prevention Methods
cards.teaser: Federal health regulators have not determined what caused a recent baby botulism outbreak or how to prevent future cases.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration continues to investigate a baby botulism outbreak without identifying its source or establishing prevention guidelines. The cases have prompted scrutiny of multiple companies, but the investigation has not yet yielded clear answers about the contamination pathway.

The three companies involved in the investigation have pointed to each other as potential sources of the outbreak. Baby botulism occurs when infants ingest spores of Clostridium botulinum bacteria, which then grow in the intestines and produce toxins. The condition can cause severe muscle weakness and breathing difficulties in infants.

cards.headline: Putin Rejects Meeting With Zelenskiy on Ukraine War
cards.teaser: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he sees no reason to meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to discuss ending the war.
cards.body:
Putin rejected Zelenskiy's offer for face-to-face talks to discuss ending the war, saying he sees "no point" in such a meeting. The Ukrainian president had written an open letter calling for direct negotiations. Speaking at the St. Petersburg economic forum, Putin described the letter as rude and refused to use Zelenskiy's name.

Putin reaffirmed Russia's war objectives, stating the country will achieve its goals in Ukraine, including seizing all of the eastern Donbas region. At the forum, business and political elites discussed whether Russia faced a choice between halting the conflict or accepting further sacrifices, but Putin's comments signaled a continuation of military operations rather than a shift toward diplomacy.

cards.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization compensation fund
cards.teaser: The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund will not continue, the Justice Department told a federal court on Friday.
cards.body:
The Justice Department confirmed in a Friday court filing that the Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund will not continue. DOJ attorneys asked the Eastern District of Virginia to reject a legal challenge to the program brought by a former federal prosecutor and others.

The fund was created to compensate individuals the administration said were targets of politically motivated investigations or prosecutions. The program drew criticism over its legal basis and funding, with challengers arguing it exceeded the administration's authority and lacked congressional authorization. The Justice Department's filing represents a reversal for one of the administration's signature initiatives.

cards.headline: EU Leaders Signal Montenegro Could Join by 2028
cards.teaser: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Montenegro is within reach of EU membership by 2028 after a Balkans summit.
cards.body:
EU leaders gathered in Montenegro to discuss accelerating the bloc's enlargement process. Von der Leyen stated that the European Union must demonstrate it is capable of and willing to take in new members, calling for the process to become "faster and more credible." German Chancellor Friedrich Merz echoed this commitment, emphasizing the need to prove the EU's ability to enlarge.

The summit brought together EU officials and representatives from six Western Balkan countries seeking membership. Von der Leyen indicated that Montenegro is "within reach" of joining by 2028, positioning it as the closest candidate nation to meeting membership requirements among those in the region.

cards.headline: Astronauts Return to ISS After Sheltering During Air Leak Repair
cards.teaser: Five astronauts returned to normal operations aboard the International Space Station after sheltering during a Russian repair attempt on a tunnel area.
cards.body:
NASA ordered five astronauts aboard the International Space Station to prepare for possible evacuation after two air leaks were discovered in the Zveda module's transfer chamber. Russian specialists detected the leaks while pressurizing the chamber during routine operations.

The crew sheltered in place as a precautionary measure while repair efforts were underway. Once work concluded, astronauts resumed normal activities on the station.

cards.headline: France Opens Investigation Into Israeli Treatment of Gaza Flotilla Activists
cards.teaser: French authorities launched an investigation into allegations that Israel mistreated pro-Palestinian flotilla activists during their detention.
cards.body:
Activists detained after Israeli forces intercepted a flotilla bound for Gaza have alleged they were mistreated while in custody. Israeli authorities have rejected these claims.

France has launched an investigation following complaints from French citizens who were among those detained during the interception. The activists were attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza when they were stopped and taken into custody.

cards.headline: Protests Grow Over Kushner-Backed Resort in Albania
cards.teaser: Days of protests have erupted over a luxury resort project on Albania's coast linked to Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump.
cards.body:
Thousands have protested in the streets of Tirana against a $1.6 billion luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner. The complex is planned for a Mediterranean area recognized as environmentally sensitive, home to 200 bird species including flamingos and Dalmatian pelicans.

Construction crews have begun erecting fences around the site, triggering public outrage over environmental damage and lack of transparency in the deal. Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama defended the project, suggesting critics would be indifferent if it weren't associated with Kushner's name.

hero.headline: Canada bans Texas cattle imports after second screwworm case confirmed
hero.body:
Canada has implemented a ban on cattle imports from Texas following confirmation of a second infected calf in the state. The action comes as Texas officials declared a state of disaster in response to the outbreak.

The screwworm is a parasitic fly larva that feeds on living tissue in warm-blooded animals. The pest was successfully eradicated from the United States in 1966 but continues to exist in parts of Central and South America. The recent cases represent the first confirmed detections in Texas in decades.

The identification of the second infected animal prompted immediate action from Canadian agricultural authorities. The import ban covers all cattle movements from Texas as officials work to contain the outbreak and prevent the parasite from spreading further across borders and regions.

Texas agriculture officials have activated response teams to survey livestock populations and establish quarantine zones around affected areas. The state's disaster declaration provides access to emergency resources and enables the rapid deployment of veterinary personnel to locations where the outbreak is occurring. Federal and state agencies are coordinating inspection protocols and developing treatment strategies to address the crisis.

The outbreak presents significant economic concerns for the Texas cattle industry, which ranks among the largest in the nation. Canada serves as a major trading partner for U.S. livestock exports, and this ban threatens to disrupt established supply chains and potentially affect market prices for cattle producers.

Authorities are focused on determining how the infestation began and implementing preventive measures to stop additional cases from occurring. The discovery of infected animals has raised concerns about the potential for broader trade restrictions from other states and countries if the outbreak cannot be quickly contained.

The screwworm's presence in the region marks a concerning development after decades without detection in the United States. The parasite's ability to infect livestock has prompted swift international response, with trading partners like Canada taking precautionary measures to protect their own herds from potential exposure.

Texas officials are working with federal agencies to coordinate a comprehensive response that addresses both the immediate threat to livestock in the state and the longer-term implications for regional cattle trade. The situation remains fluid as investigation and containment efforts continue.

The ban highlights the interconnected nature of North American agriculture and how disease outbreaks in one region can quickly affect trade relationships and economic activity across borders. Officials emphasize the importance of rapid detection and response protocols in managing livestock health crises that could have far-reaching consequences for the industry.

cards.headline: Park ranger dies after falling into crevasse on Denali
cards.teaser: A National Park Service climbing ranger died after falling into a crevasse during a patrol on Mount McKinley in Alaska.
cards.body:
A park ranger died after falling into a crevasse on Denali, North America's tallest peak. The ranger was conducting a patrol on Mount McKinley when the accident occurred.

The death marks the fourth fatality of the climbing season on the mountain. The National Park Service confirmed the ranger was an employee conducting official duties at the time of the fall. Denali presents extreme hazards to climbers, including hidden crevasses, severe weather, and high altitude conditions.

cards.headline: Virginia man sentenced to life for plotting wife's murder with au pair
cards.teaser: Brendan Banfield received a life sentence for scheming with his family's au pair to kill his wife in a case that also involved the death of a stranger.
cards.body:
A Virginia man has been sentenced to life in prison without parole for the murders of his wife and another man. Brendan Banfield, a former IRS law enforcement officer, was convicted of orchestrating the killings with his family's Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães, with whom he was having an affair.

Banfield claimed he shot Joseph Ryan in self-defense after discovering Ryan attacking his wife on February 24, 2023. However, prosecutors proved that Banfield and the au pair had set up Ryan as a fall guy in their scheme to murder Christine Banfield, a pediatric intensive care nurse.

cards.headline: Justice Department argues courts cannot block White House ballroom construction
cards.teaser: Federal lawyers told an appeals court that no judicial authority exists to stop construction of a ballroom at the White House, even comparing presidential power to hypothetically demolishing national monuments.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has asked a federal appeals court to overturn a lower court decision blocking construction of a $400 million ballroom at the White House. A Justice Department lawyer argued that no court has the authority to halt the project, claiming only Congress could stop it.

The ballroom would be built on the site of the White House's demolished East Wing. A secure underground bunker at the location has been allowed to proceed while the legal dispute continues between Washington DC preservationists and the White House over the project.

cards.headline: Iranian national soccer team receives US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Officials confirmed that Iran's football team has been granted entry visas to compete in the World Cup, just days before their opening match in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Iran's football team has been granted visas to enter the United States for World Cup participation. The approval arrives just 10 days before the team's opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles.

The visa decision clears the way for Iranian players and staff to compete in their scheduled World Cup fixtures on U.S. soil.

cards.headline: US military shoots down Iranian drones over Persian Gulf
cards.teaser: American forces intercepted Iranian drones launched toward Gulf allies in the latest military exchange as the Trump administration pursues negotiations with Tehran.
cards.body:
The U.S. military shot down Iranian drones that were launched toward American allies in the Persian Gulf. The U.S. also struck Iranian drone facilities and radar installations in response.

Iran retaliated by targeting American military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain. The exchange marks another escalation as the Trump administration increases pressure on Iran to reach an agreement to end hostilities in the region.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 Finals lead with one-point victory over Spurs
cards.teaser: New York defeated San Antonio to move within two wins of the franchise's first NBA championship in over 50 years.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 in Game 2 of the NBA Finals, extending their series lead to 2-0. The thrilling matchup came down to the final moments, with the Knicks securing the one-point victory.

The series now moves to New York, where the Knicks need two more wins to claim their first championship in generations. The red-hot team returns home with a commanding advantage in the best-of-seven series.

cards.body:
The Nasdaq Composite declined 4.2 percent on Friday, marking its worst single day of the year. The S&P 500 also posted its worst performance of 2026, with broad losses across Wall Street as chip stocks fell sharply.

The selloff intensified following strong jobs data that raised expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases. Technology and AI-related stocks bore the brunt of the decline as investors reassessed valuations in the sector amid shifting economic conditions.

cards.headline: States preparing lawsuit to block Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros
cards.teaser: Multiple US states are preparing antitrust litigation to prevent the merger of two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
US states are preparing a lawsuit to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros, according to sources familiar with the matter. The action would add to legal challenges already facing the merger between the two major film and television studios.

Warner Bros Discovery shares fell on reports of the anticipated state antitrust challenge. A Paramount lawyer claimed that opponents of the deal hold antisemitic views, according to court filings. The company has asked a court to dismiss an existing lawsuit seeking to block the transaction.

cards.headline: Google to pay SpaceX $920 million monthly in cloud computing agreement
cards.teaser: Google signed a major deal to purchase computing capacity from SpaceX data centers in a partnership valued at nearly $1 billion per month.
cards.body:
Google will pay SpaceX $920 million per month for compute capacity at xAI data centers under a new cloud computing deal. The agreement represents one of the largest technology infrastructure partnerships announced this year and comes ahead of SpaceX's planned initial public offering.

The deal will provide Google with access to AI computing resources as demand for such capacity grows across the technology industry. SpaceX recently secured a similar computing pact with Anthropic. The monthly payments will provide SpaceX with substantial recurring revenue as it prepares to enter public markets.

cards.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 to lowest level since October 2024
cards.teaser: Bitcoin dropped to its lowest price in nearly two years as strong employment data and technical issues in cryptocurrency markets added pressure.
cards.body:
Bitcoin fell below $60,000, reaching its lowest level since October 2024 as cryptocurrency markets came under pressure. The decline came alongside strong jobs data that increased expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases, as well as a bug affecting Zcash that contributed to broader crypto market volatility.

Investors have increasingly shifted focus toward AI stocks and large initial public offerings, with some analysts suggesting bitcoin's prominence has faded. The cryptocurrency has lost significant value from its previous highs as traditional financial assets have attracted more investor attention.

cards.headline: Anthropic calls for option to pause AI development globally
cards.teaser: The AI company warned that systems will soon be able to improve themselves without human intervention and urged consideration of a development pause.
cards.body:
Anthropic urged world leaders to create an option for pausing AI development, warning that artificial intelligence will soon reach the capability to improve itself without human intervention. The company flagged self-improvement as a significant risk that could emerge in advanced AI systems.

The proposal has generated debate among technology experts and policymakers about how to manage AI safety concerns. Anthropic's warning comes as multiple AI companies race to develop more powerful systems, raising questions about appropriate safeguards and international coordination on AI development.

cards.headline: S&P 500 index delays entry for SpaceX and other large recent IPOs
cards.teaser: Major companies that went public recently may wait years before joining the benchmark index under existing eligibility rules.
cards.body:
SpaceX and other companies with major initial public offerings may not join the S&P 500 index for years, despite their significant market size. The index's administrators have rules requiring companies to demonstrate sustained profitability before inclusion. SpaceX currently operates at substantial losses despite its high valuation.

The S&P 500 has introduced fast-track provisions for older companies going public, but these do not apply to all recent IPOs regardless of their market capitalization. This decision also affects OpenAI and Anthropic, preventing their potential near-term entry into the benchmark.

hero.headline: LinkedIn Co-Founder Reid Hoffman Steps Down from Microsoft Board to Focus on AI Startup
hero.body:
Reid Hoffman has announced his departure from Microsoft's board of directors after ten years to dedicate himself to leading Manus, an artificial intelligence startup focused on drug discovery. The LinkedIn co-founder's decision reflects what some in the technology industry describe as "founder mode," a shift toward direct operational involvement rather than board-level oversight.

Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn in 2002 and served as its chief executive before Microsoft acquired the professional networking platform in 2016 for $26.2 billion. Throughout his tenure on Microsoft's board, which coincided with major company transformations including its shift to cloud computing and recent artificial intelligence investments, board members received substantial compensation through cash and stock grants.

His move to step down signals a departure from governance responsibilities at one of the world's largest technology companies. Instead of maintaining a primarily advisory or investor role, Hoffman is positioning himself for hands-on leadership at Manus. The timing underscores his commitment to the startup during a period when artificial intelligence applications in drug discovery have attracted significant venture capital funding as machine learning capabilities have advanced.

Hoffman has maintained an active involvement in the technology sector beyond his board seat. He continues as an investor and stakeholder through Greylock Partners, his venture capital firm, while pursuing other business ventures in the AI space. His decision to leave Microsoft comes as the company continues navigating its evolving role in artificial intelligence development and deployment.

Microsoft has not yet announced a replacement for Hoffman's board position. The company will need to identify a successor to fill the vacancy created by his departure.

Hoffman's focus on Manus represents a broader trend among seasoned technology entrepreneurs who choose to redirect their energies toward startups rather than remain in purely governance roles at established corporations. His background as a founder and executive positions him with the operational experience many high-growth startups require during critical development phases.

The pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries have increasingly turned to machine learning and artificial intelligence to streamline drug discovery processes, potentially reducing both development timelines and costs. This sector has become an attractive destination for venture capital investment and experienced technology leaders seeking to apply computational advances to healthcare challenges.

Hoffman's departure from Microsoft's board marks a significant transition in his career trajectory, reflecting a preference for direct involvement in building new ventures over continuing participation in the governance of an already-established technology giant. His focus on Manus will likely intensify as he dedicates himself fully to the startup's growth and development in the competitive field of AI-driven drug discovery.

cards.headline: Startup Founders Share Venture Capital Horror Stories in Viral Discussion
cards.teaser: A widespread conversation on social media platform X has gathered accounts from founders describing negative experiences with venture capital firms.
cards.body:
Entrepreneurs have launched a viral conversation on X this week, sharing negative experiences with venture capital investors. The discussion includes both unusual and infuriating accounts, with some founders publicly identifying specific firms and individuals involved in their interactions.

The public airing of these grievances marks a notable departure from the typically confidential nature of founder-investor relationships. Venture capital firms invest in early-stage companies in exchange for equity stakes, granting them considerable influence over business operations and strategy.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with Revelation in Spring 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix announced that Final Fantasy VII: Revelation will complete the remake trilogy of the classic game, with a release scheduled for spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation, the final installment in its remake trilogy, at Summer Game Fest Live. The game will release simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027. A debut trailer showcased gameplay footage from the upcoming title.

The remake trilogy modernizes the 1997 original with updated graphics and expanded narrative. The first two games, Final Fantasy VII Remake and Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, launched in 2020 and 2024 respectively.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 Announced for PC and PlayStation 5 with Beta Planned for Fall 2027
cards.teaser: ArenaNet revealed Guild Wars 3 at Summer Game Fest, marking a new chapter for the massively multiplayer online role-playing game franchise.
cards.body:
The developer announced Guild Wars 3 will launch on PC and PlayStation 5, with a beta test scheduled for fall 2027. The game represents what the company describes as a modern evolution of the MMORPG genre. ArenaNet released a trailer showcasing the new title at the Summer Game Fest event.

Guild Wars 2, the current game in the franchise, continues to operate with its player base intact. The original Guild Wars launched in 2005, and Guild Wars 2 followed in 2012. The franchise has maintained a following in the competitive MMORPG market dominated by titles like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV.

cards.headline: Diver Discovers Unusual Fish, Solving 20-Year Scientific Mystery
cards.teaser: A diver's encounter with a hairy-looking fish provided the answer to a question that had puzzled marine researchers for two decades.
cards.body:
A recreational diver spotted an unusual fish species covered in hair-like structures during an underwater expedition. The sighting resolved a 20-year mystery that marine biologists had been unable to solve through other means.

The discovery highlights the role amateur divers can play in advancing scientific knowledge about ocean life. Many marine species remain poorly documented, particularly those living in remote or deep-water environments that scientists visit infrequently.

hero.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead in NBA Finals with last-second win over Spurs
hero.body:
The New York Knicks moved within two wins of their first NBA championship since 1970, defeating the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 in Game 2 of the NBA Finals. The victory gives the Knicks a commanding 2-0 series lead as the Finals shift to Madison Square Garden for Game 3.

The game came down to the final moments, with Jalen Brunson sinking the go-ahead free throw with 9.5 seconds remaining after Victor Wembanyama committed a turnover. Wembanyama then had a clean look from the elbow at the buzzer, but the shot caromed off the back rim. This victory made the Knicks only the third team to win the first two games of an NBA Finals on the road, joining the 1993 Chicago Bulls and the 1995 Houston Rockets.

Brunson continued his standout performance in crucial moments, leading the Knicks' offense through another clutch game. The All-NBA guard has been instrumental in the team's success, particularly in close contests. After stealing Game 1 with a furious fourth-quarter comeback, the Knicks demonstrated their ability to win in hostile environments.

Josh Hart made an unusual impact in Game 2, with what was described as a quiet statistical performance by his standards. Despite his lower numbers, Hart's teammates praised his willingness to adapt to whatever the team needed. He matched a Finals record previously held by Larry Bird in the game.

The Knicks are riding exceptional momentum heading into Game 3. The team has won 11 consecutive games, many by substantial margins, and brings a fresh appearance with a week of rest before the Finals began. Their defense has been particularly strong, posting the best defensive net rating of the NBA playoffs, which could prove crucial against the Spurs' young core.

The Spurs face an uphill battle returning to New York. No team has ever overcome a 3-0 deficit in the NBA Finals, making Game 3 critical for San Antonio's championship hopes. Coming off a physically demanding series against the Oklahoma City Thunder, the Spurs may be dealing with fatigue as they attempt their comeback.

Wembanyama, the young star who has drawn attention from various figures, will need to bounce back from his missed final shot. The 7-foot-4 generational talent remains a constant scoring and blocking threat for San Antonio.

Game 3 at Madison Square Garden will take place under heightened security measures. The venue has implemented a ban on all bags for the game as part of enhanced security protocols related to high-profile attendance. The atmosphere is expected to be intense as the Knicks attempt to take control of the series in front of their home fans.

cards.headline: Teenager Andreeva faces qualifier Chwalinska in French Open final
cards.teaser: Two contrasting paths lead to Saturday's French Open final, where a teenage star meets an unexpected qualifier.
cards.body:
Mirra Andreeva and Maja Chwalinska will contest the French Open final on Saturday. Andreeva is a teenage star who has long been expected to win a Grand Slam title, while Chwalinska is a qualifier who has emerged as an unexpected contender.

The final represents a clash between two contrasting narratives—Andreeva's anticipated rise to the top of tennis against Chwalinska's surprising breakthrough performance on one of the sport's biggest stages.

cards.headline: Browns trade All-Pro Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and three draft picks
cards.teaser: The Cleveland Browns have dealt star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a major offseason trade.
cards.body:
The Browns traded Myles Garrett to the Rams in exchange for defensive player Jared Verse and three draft picks. The deal represents a significant shift for both franchises, with Los Angeles acquiring an All-Pro pass rusher and Cleveland receiving a younger player plus future draft capital.

The trade alters the landscape for NFL contenders heading into the upcoming season. The Rams are incorporating Garrett into their defensive scheme, while the Browns rebuild their defensive line around Verse and prepare to use their additional draft picks.

cards.headline: Iran national team receives US visas for World Cup with 10 days until opener
cards.teaser: Iranian players have been granted visas to enter the United States for the World Cup, though many staff members were denied entry.
cards.body:
Iran's football team has been granted visas to enter the United States for the World Cup. The approval comes just 10 days before their opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles.

However, many members of Iran's staff were denied visas and will not be able to accompany the squad to the tournament.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses World Cup water bottle ban after backlash
cards.teaser: FIFA changed its policy to allow fans to bring disposable water bottles into World Cup stadiums after facing criticism.
cards.body:
FIFA has reversed its ban on disposable water bottles in World Cup stadiums. Fans will now be permitted to bring water bottles into matches during the tournament.

The governing body had initially prohibited disposable bottles from stadiums, but reversed the policy following widespread criticism. Many viewed the restriction as impractical for outdoor summer matches being held across North American host cities.

cards.headline: Caleb Williams featured on Madden 27 cover in homage to Michael Jordan
cards.teaser: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams appears on the cover of Madden NFL 27, drawing inspiration from basketball legend Michael Jordan.
cards.body:
Caleb Williams was named the cover athlete for Madden NFL 27, with his cover design paying tribute to Michael Jordan. The Bears quarterback said he was eager to win as many games as possible with Chicago in the upcoming season.

The selection represents another milestone for Williams as he enters his professional career. The cover design connects two Chicago sports icons, linking Williams' football career to Jordan's basketball legacy in the city.

cards.headline: Harry Kane described as irreplaceable for England ahead of World Cup
cards.teaser: England's captain enters the World Cup with observers questioning whether this tournament will establish him as the world's best player.
cards.body:
Harry Kane has been described as irreplaceable for England as the national team prepares for World Cup competition. The striker, who is also a Ballon d'Or contender, faces questions about whether this tournament will provide the platform to prove he is the best player in the world.

Kane enters the competition as England's captain and primary attacking threat. His performance in the upcoming matches could define both England's tournament prospects and his own legacy on the international stage.

hero.headline: Actor Anthony Head Dies, Buffy the Vampire Slayer Cast Pay Tribute
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," his daughters Emily and Daisy Head said in a statement.

Head portrayed Giles, the school librarian and mentor to Sarah Michelle Gellar's vampire slayer, throughout the series' seven-season run from 1997 to 2003. The character became one of the most beloved figures in the show, guiding Buffy Summers through her supernatural battles with wisdom, humor, and emotional depth.

Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute to Head on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She continued: "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Beyond Buffy, Head enjoyed a lengthy career spanning several decades. He was perhaps best known in the UK and US for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements, which featured a slow-burn courtship between a British couple. He also appeared in the BBC sketch show Little Britain as a prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant, played by David Walliams.

Head took on additional roles in the BBC production of Merlin, and more recently appeared in Ted Lasso, where he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion and worked alongside co-creator Jason Sudeikis. His film work included appearances in The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie.

His career began on the stage, where he starred in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell. He later played Freddie Trumper in the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988, and performed as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show. In the early 1980s, he also sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box.

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father founded Verity Films and worked as a documentary filmmaker, while his mother was an actress who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret.

During Buffy's production, Head commuted between Los Angeles and England, where his partner Sarah and two daughters lived. "I'd try to go home to them every three or four weeks," he told the Guardian. "I spent quite a lot of money on airfares, but we made it work."

His daughters noted that Head loved his work and considered himself fortunate to have worked with talented people across productions spanning several decades. "His legacy will live on in the shows he was a part of and in the audiences that love them," they said.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy Killed in Tarzana Stabbing, Murder Charges Filed
cards.teaser: Veteran actor James Handy was fatally stabbed at a Tarzana residence, and his girlfriend's son has been charged with murder.
cards.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old veteran actor known for roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji, died after being stabbed at his home in Tarzana, Los Angeles. He was found unconscious in his front yard on Wednesday with multiple stab wounds to his chest and was pronounced dead at the hospital.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested and charged with murder. Court proceedings have been temporarily paused while the suspect undergoes a mental competency examination.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Releases Toy Story 5 Song and Music Video
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift's song for Toy Story 5 has been released with a music video featuring the character Jessie and has broken multiple streaming records.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift wrote and released "I Knew It, I Knew You" for the upcoming Toy Story 5 film, featuring a music video with footage of Jessie, the cowgirl character voiced by Joan Cusack. The song showcases Swift's return to her country roots with a rootsy, handcrafted style that fans appreciate.

In creating the track, Swift acknowledged the legacy of Randy Newman's iconic Toy Story songs, particularly "When She Loved Me" from Toy Story 2. The release generated significant streaming success upon debut and was rolled out as part of the promotional campaign for Pixar's fifth installment in the beloved animated franchise.

cards.headline: Rock Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: Greg James, a tattoo artist known for his work with rock musicians, has died at the age of 71.
cards.body:
Greg James, a tattoo artist who became known for his work with numerous rock music figures, died at age 71. James built a career tattooing musicians and became recognized within the rock music community for his artistry.

James was considered a go-to tattoo artist for rock performers over several decades. His death was confirmed by multiple sources, though the specific cause was reported by some outlets.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skipped Oscars for Mental Health Reasons
cards.teaser: Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor at the Academy Awards but did not attend the ceremony, citing mental health concerns.
cards.body:
Sean Penn won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for his role in One Battle After Another but was not present at the ceremony to accept the award. Penn later stated that he skipped the event for mental health reasons.

The actor also revealed his dislike of selfies during recent comments. Penn's absence from the Oscars came despite winning one of the evening's major acting awards. The statuette was accepted on his behalf during the broadcast.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Remake Trilogy to Conclude with Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the final game in its remake trilogy, set to launch in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII: Revelation as the third and final installment in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy. The game launches in spring 2027 across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

The announcement included a first trailer shown at Summer Game Fest Live. The remake trilogy has expanded and reimagined the original 1997 PlayStation game across multiple entries for contemporary platforms.

cards.headline: Among Us Animated Series Releases on Paramount Plus
cards.teaser: An animated television adaptation of Among Us has been released on Paramount Plus with all 10 episodes available immediately.
cards.body:
The animated Among Us television series dropped on Paramount Plus without advance warning, with all 10 episodes of the first season available for streaming. The surprise announcement was made by series stars Yvette Nicole Brown and Liv Hewson at the Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles.

The show is based on the popular multiplayer video game Among Us, which became a cultural phenomenon during 2020. The series had not been heavily promoted prior to its release, making the drop a genuine surprise for fans of the game.

hero.headline: DOGE proposal would have incorrectly marked 2.7 million people as dead
hero.teaser: A whistleblower alleges a plan to mark millions of living people as deceased was part of an immigration enforcement effort.
hero.body:
A proposal would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead, according to allegations from a whistleblower. The plan was reportedly part of a broader immigration enforcement push.

The whistleblower's account raises questions about the accuracy and consequences of the proposed database changes. Incorrectly marking millions of people as deceased could have affected their access to government services, employment verification, and legal status.

cards.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization compensation fund
cards.teaser: The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund will not continue, the Justice Department told a federal court on Friday.
cards.body:
The Justice Department confirmed in a Friday court filing that the Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund will not continue. DOJ attorneys asked the Eastern District of Virginia to reject a legal challenge to the program brought by a former federal prosecutor and others.

The fund was created to compensate individuals the administration said were targets of politically motivated investigations or prosecutions. The program drew criticism over its legal basis and funding, with challengers arguing it exceeded the administration's authority and lacked congressional authorization. The Justice Department's filing represents a reversal for one of the administration's signature initiatives.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra takes lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra secured the top spot in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra has secured the top spot on California's November general election ballot for governor. The Democratic candidate mounted a come-from-behind primary victory in what has been one of California's most turbulent campaign seasons in recent memory.

Election officials are still counting millions of ballots to determine Becerra's general election opponent. His potential challengers include fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who has advocated for universal healthcare and higher taxes on billionaires, and Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality who received Donald Trump's endorsement.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Her victory advances her to the November general election.

If elected, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

cards.headline: Chief of staff to Texas congressman charged with firearm violations
cards.teaser: Luis Vega, chief of staff for Representative Pete Sessions, faces charges related to allegedly bringing a gun into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, chief of staff for Representative Pete Sessions of Texas, was charged with two firearm counts on Wednesday. The charges stem from an alleged incident in which Vega attempted to bring a firearm into the U.S. Capitol complex days before Christmas last year.

Vega serves as the top staffer for the Republican congressman. The charges were filed months after the alleged December incident at the Capitol.

cards.headline: Trump discusses farm prices and Washington fountains at event
cards.teaser: The president acknowledged economic pressures on farmers while supporters cheered for ending the war.
cards.body:
President Trump spoke about higher fertilizer and fuel prices affecting farmers during an event where supporters expressed support for ending the war. The president acknowledged the price pressures facing agricultural producers.

Trump also spent significant time discussing Washington infrastructure, including the city's fountains and the Reflecting Pool. Attendees at the event demonstrated enthusiasm for the administration's stance on concluding military operations.

cards.headline: New York legislature passes data center and consumer protection bills
cards.teaser: Three bills regulating data centers, surveillance pricing, and digital stalking passed both chambers and await the governor's signature.
cards.body:
The New York State Senate and Assembly passed three bills addressing data centers, surveillance pricing, and digital stalking. The legislation now heads to Governor Kathy Hochul for her signature.

The package includes a moratorium on certain data center activities and new consumer protections. Lawmakers did not advance other proposed measures on environmental policy, housing, and entertainment during the current session.
